filing.source_excerpt: Item 1.01. Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. On October 25, 2026, Range Resources Corporation, a Delaware corporation (“ Range ”), entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “ Merger Agreement ”) with EQT Corporation, a Pennsylvania corporation (“ EQT ”), EQT Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of EQT, Rhino Merger Sub Inc., a Delaware corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of EQT (“ Merger Sub ”), and Rhino Merger Sub LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of EQT (“ LLC Sub ”). Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, which has been unanimously approved by the board of directors of Range and the board of directors of EQT (the “ EQT Board ”), Merger Sub will merge with and into Range (the “ First Merger ”), with Range surviving as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of EQT (the “ First Step Surviving Corporation ”), and as the second step in a single integrated transaction with the First Merger, the First Step Surviving Corporation will merge with and into LLC Sub (the “ Second Merger ” and, together with the First Merger, the “ Mergers ”), with LLC Sub surviving the Second Merger as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of EQT. At the effective time of the First Merger (the “ Effective Time ”), among other things, each share of common stock, par value $0.01 per share, of Range (“ Range Common Stock ”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (including Range restricted stock awards but excluding Excluded Shares (as defined in the Merger Agreement)) will be converted into the right to receive, without interest, 0.987 (the “ Exchange Ratio ”) shares of common stock, no par value, of EQT (“ EQT Common Stock ”). Cash will be paid in lieu of any fractional shares of EQT Common Stock that otherwise would have been issued to any Range stockholder in the Mergers. Following the closing of the Mergers (the “ Closing ”), Range’s existing stockholders and EQT’s existing stockholders will own approximately 27% and 73%, respectively, of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Governance In the Merger Agreement, EQT has agreed to increase the size of the EQT Board to 12 members and appoint Dennis L. Degner and one other individual selected by Range (who shall satisfy the independence requirements of the New York Stock Exchange (the “ NYSE ”) with respect to service on the EQT Board), after reasonable consultation with EQT and with the consent of EQT (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed) (the “ Range Designees ”), to the EQT Board at the Effective Time. EQT has also agreed that, following the Closing, EQT will take all necessary action to nominate the Range Designees for election to the EQT Board at the first annual meeting of shareholders of EQT thereafter. Conditions to the Mergers The completion of the First Merger is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain closing conditions, including (i) the adoption of the Merger Agreement by the holders of a majority of the voting power of the outstanding shares of Range Common Stock entitled to vote thereon (the “ Range Stockholder Approval ”) at a special meeting of Range stockholders to be held in connection with the Mergers (including any adjournments or postponements thereof, the “ Range Stockholders’ Meeting ”), (ii) the approval of the issuance of the shares of EQT Common Stock in connection with the First Merger (such shares, the “ EQT Shares ” and such issuance, the “ Share Issuance ”) by a majority of the votes cast (the “ EQT Shareholder Approval ”) at a special meeting of EQT shareholders to be held in connection with the Mergers (including any adjournments or postponements thereof, the “ EQT Shareholders’ Meeting ”), (iii) the EQT Shares being approved for listing on the NYSE, (iv) there being no law, injunction, order or decree prohibiting consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement (the “ Transactions ”), (v) the expiration or termination of (a) all waiting periods (and any extensions thereof) applicable to the Transactions under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, and (b) any commitment to, or any agreement with, any governmental entity to delay the consummation of the Transactions or to not consummate the Transactions before a certain date (such condition, the “ HSR Act Condition ”), (vi) the effectiveness of the registration statement on Form S-4 to be filed by EQT with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC ”) pursuant to which the EQT Shares will be registered, (vii) no Company Material Adverse Effect and no Parent Material Adverse Effect (each as defined in the Merger Agreement) having occurred since the date of the Merger Agreement, and (viii) subject to certain materiality qualifications and exceptions, the accuracy of each party’s representations and warranties and each party’s compliance with, or waiver of its obligations under, if permissible, its covenants in the Merger Agreement. memos_so_far.headline: Range Resources agrees to be acquired by EQT, all stock, 0.987 EQT share per RRC share; RRC holders get 27% of the combined company
reasoning: Source: Range's 8-K filed 07:07 ET, item 1.01. Quoted: 'each share of common stock ... of Range ... will be converted into the right to receive, without interest, 0.987 (the "Exchange Ratio") shares of common stock, no par value, of EQT'. Also: 'Range's existing stockholders and EQT's existing stockholders will own approximately 27% and 73%, respectively, of the combined company'.

Approvals: 'unanimously approved by the board of directors of Range and the board of directors of EQT'. Conditions include votes at both companies and no injunction. Benzinga gives expected closing as Q1 2027.

Timing: the first Benzinga report was at 06:03 ET (10:03 UTC), about an hour before the 8-K. Both came before the open, and no session has traded it. There was no earlier rumor in Benzinga's last ten days.
What changed: Range stops being an independent Appalachian gas producer. Its share value is now tied to EQT's share price at a fixed ratio.

Pre-market on IEX: RRC has no prints yet against its 45.535 close. EQT trades at 51.52, -7.4% from 55.62, on 6,327 shares. At that price the ratio is worth 50.85 per RRC share, +11.7%; at Friday's EQT close it was 54.90.

memos_so_far.headline: No mispricing to trade: RRC's price is now set mechanically at 0.987 x EQT less an arbitrage spread
reasoning: What changed: Range's value no longer depends on its own gas output. It is 0.987 EQT shares, payable in about five months (Q1 2027 close) if both votes pass and there is no injunction.

Long RRC: at the open RRC will gap to the ratio's value less the usual arbitrage spread, a few percent for an all-stock deal with antitrust review between two large Appalachian producers. From an entry after that gap, the upside is the spread narrowing over months, not 5-10 trading days. The downside is EQT falling further or the deal breaking. No edge at our horizon.

Short EQT, the acquirer: the market has already marked it down 7.4% pre-market (6,327 IEX shares, a real volume for pre-market). Arbitrage funds shorting EQT against long RRC add pressure, but that is the known mechanism and it is in the pre-market price. Betting on more downside is guessing the size of a reaction that has already happened.

What the market would have to be wrong about: either the deal's completion odds (no information to say so) or EQT's fair value after issuing about 27% of the combined company (the 7.4% drop is close to what a full-premium, all-stock deal usually costs a buyer). Neither gives a thesis I can defend.

Would prove this wrong: RRC trading well below 0.987 x EQT through the week (a spread of 8% or more) with no deal-risk news. That would mean the market doubts the close, which would be a separate case.
objections: Merger-arbitrage pricing, not mispricing; any edge is a months-long spread, outside a 10-day horizon.
